arxiv-2104-12217.title: On the transport equation for probability density functions of turbulent vorticity fields
arxiv-2104-12217.creator: Jiawei Li, Zhongmin Qian, Mingrui Zhou
arxiv-2104-12217.description: Abstract Vorticity random fields of turbulent flows (modeled over the vorticity equation with random initial data for example) are singled out as the main dynamic variables for the description of turbulence, and the evolution equation of the probability density function (PDF) of the vorticity field has been obtained.

arxiv-2107-01768.title: Tits groups of Iwahori-Weyl groups and presentations of Hecke algebras
arxiv-2107-01768.creator: Radhika Ganapathy, Xuhua He
arxiv-2107-01768.description: Abstract . Let G G be a connected reductive group over a non-archimedean local field F F and I I be an Iwahori subgroup of G ⁡ ( F ) G(F) . Let I n I_{n} is the n n -th Moy-Prasad filtration subgroup of I I .

arxiv-2202-06918.title: The Habitable Zones of Rapidly Rotating Main Sequence A/F Stars
arxiv-2202-06918.creator: John P. Ahlers, Emeline F. Fromont, Ravi Kopparappu, P. Wilson Cauley, Jacob Haqq-Misra
arxiv-2202-06918.description: Abstract We investigate how rapid stellar rotation commonly seen in A/F stars can influence planet habitability. Specifically, we model how rapid rotation influences a planet’s irradiation and determine the location of the habitable zone for stars in the mass range 1.3 ​ M ⊙ ≤ M ⋆ ≤ 2.2 ​ M ⊙ 1.3M_{\odot}\leq M_{\star}\leq 2.2M_{\odot} .

arxiv-2205-09479.title: Neural ODEs with Irregular and Noisy Data
arxiv-2205-09479.creator: Pawan Goyal, Peter Benner
arxiv-2205-09479.description: Abstract Measurement noise is an integral part while collecting data of a physical process. Thus, noise removal is necessary to draw conclusions from these data, and it often becomes essential to construct dynamical models using these data. We discuss a methodology to learn differential equation(s) using noisy and irregular sampled measurements.

arxiv-2311-02223.title: Landau-Lifshitz-Navier-Stokes Equations: Large Deviations and Relationship to The Energy Equality
arxiv-2311-02223.creator: Benjamin Gess, Daniel Heydecker, Zhengyan Wu
arxiv-2311-02223.description: Abstract . The dynamical large deviations principle for the three-dimensional incompressible Landau-Lifschitz-Navier-Stokes equations is shown, in the joint scaling regime of vanishing noise intensity and correlation length. This proves the consistency of the large deviations in lattice gas models [ QY98 ] , with Landau-Lifschitz fluctuating hydrodynamics [ LL87 ] .

arxiv-2412-13878.title: Benchmarking Quantum Models for Time-series Forecasting Thanks: Work done as part of the QCHALLenge project funded by Bundesministerium für Wirtschaft und Klimaschutz
arxiv-2412-13878.creator: Caitlin Jones, Maximilian Adler, Nico Kraus, Michael Schrödl-Baumann, Pallavi Bhardwaj, David Zambrano Manrique
arxiv-2412-13878.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Caitlin Jones, Maximilian Adler, Nico Kraus, Michael Schrödl-Baumann, Pallavi Bhardwaj, David Zambrano Manrique. Time series forecasting is a valuable tool for many applications, such as stock price predictions, demand forecasting or logistical optimization. There are many well-established statistical and machine learning models that are used for this purpose. Recently in the field of quantum machine learning many candidate models for forecasting have been proposed, however in the absence of theoretical grounds for advantage thorough benchmarking is essential for scientific evaluation.

arxiv-2510-22604.title: Geometric Dynamical Systems
arxiv-2510-22604.creator: Ghorbanali Haghighatdoost
arxiv-2510-22604.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Ghorbanali Haghighatdoost. This article provides a conceptual and historical review of the evolution of integrable Hamiltonian systems from the Moscow School of A. Fomenko to the emerging Azarbaijan School of Geometric Dynamical Systems founded by the author. Beginning with the topological classification of integrable systems through Liouville foliations, atoms, and molecular invariants, the paper traces how these geometric ideas evolved into modern frameworks based on Lie groupoids, Lie algebroids, and fractional calculus.

arxiv-2512-06406.title: UncertaintyZoo : An Uncertainty Quantification Toolkit for Large Language Models
arxiv-2512-06406.creator: Xianzong Wu, Xiaohong Li, Lili Quan, Qiang Hu
arxiv-2512-06406.description: Abstract . Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly expanding their real-world applications across domains, e.g., question answering, autonomous driving, and automatic software development. Despite this achievement, LLMs, as data-driven systems, often make incorrect predictions, which can lead to potential losses in safety-critical scenarios.

pmc-10574062.title: Dietary Patterns, Socio-Demographic Predictors Thereof, and Associations of Dietary Patterns with Stunting and Overweight/Obesity in 1–<10-Year-Old Children in Two Economically Active Provinces in South Africa
pmc-10574062.creator: Marjanne Senekal, Johanna H Nel, Gabriel Eksteen, Nelia P Steyn, Chara Tzavara, Charalampia Amerikanou, Andriana Kaliora
pmc-10574062.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2023). A review of the literature showed that there were only a few studies that reported on the dietary patterns of children in South Africa. The aim of the present study was to characterise the dietary patterns of children aged 1–<10 years who were studied during the Provincial Dietary Intake Survey (PDIS) in 2018 and to investigate the socio-demographic predictors thereof, as well as the associations with stunting and overweight/obesity.

pmc-10647285.title: A Multi-Model Based Stability Analysis Employing Multi-Environmental Trials (METs) Data for Discerning Heat Tolerance in Chickpea (Cicer arietinum L.) Landraces
pmc-10647285.creator: Thippeswamy Danakumara, Tapan Kumar, Neeraj Kumar, Basavanagouda Siddanagouda Patil, Chellapilla Bharadwaj, Umashankar Patel, Nilesh Joshi, Shayla Bindra, Shailesh Tripathi, Rajeev Kumar Varshney, Sushil Kumar Chaturvedi, Zhaoshi Xu
pmc-10647285.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2023). Identifying a congenially targeted production environment and understanding the effects of genotype by environmental interactions on the adaption of chickpea genotypes is essential for achieving an optimal yield stability. Different models like additive main effect and multiplicative interactions (AMMI 1, AMM2), weighted average absolute scores of BLUPs (WAASB), and genotype plus genotype–environment (GGE) interactions were used to understand their suitability in the precise estimation of variance and their interaction. Our experiment used genotypes that represent the West Asia–North Africa (WANA) region.

pmc-11337763.title: Threats of nursing productivity in the digital era: investigating the interplay between smartphones addiction and procrastination behavior among nurses
pmc-11337763.creator: Ahmed Abdelwahab Ibrahim El-Sayed, Shimaa Fathy Daif Allah Goda, Gehan Galal Elbialy
pmc-11337763.description: BackgroundControlling smartphone addiction and procrastination among nurses is crucial for enhancing the productivity of both nursing and the healthcare system. Critical care nurses are highly vulnerable to smartphone addiction and procrastination behaviors than other groups. They may purposefully delay their tasks, a practice known as active procrastination, or inadvertently delay them, a practice known as passive procrastination.

pmc-11676068.title: Effects of Biological Nitrogen Fixation and Nitrogen Deposition on Soil Microbial Communities in Karst Grassland Ecosystems
pmc-11676068.creator: Xin Liu, Rong Yang, Jie Zhao, Dan Xiao, Xunyang He, Wei Zhang, Kelin Wang, Hongsong Chen
pmc-11676068.description: Diverse exogenous nitrogen (N) sources have a considerable impact on microbial community structure in terrestrial ecosystems. Legume plants and N deposition can relieve N limitations and increase net primary productivity. However, the differences in their effects on soil microbial communities remain unclear.

pmc-12374718.title: A Novel Integrated Approach: Plant-Mediated Synthesis, in vitro and in silico Evaluation of Silver Nanoparticles for Breast Cancer and Bacterial Therapies
pmc-12374718.creator: Sahar S Alghamdi, Haifa A Alhaidal, Afrah E Mohammed, Arwa Alsubait, Maali D Alshammari, Lamis Alsaqer, Shahad Saleem Alzahrani, Fai Alanazi, Layan Basel Al Tuhayni, Rizwan Ali, Shaden Alharbi, Bader Hazazi, Mona E AlEnazi, Zeyad I Alehaideb
pmc-12374718.description: Background and AimNanotechnology offers a promising approach to address breast cancer and bacterial resistance, two critical global health challenges. This study synthesized silver nanoparticles (AgNPs) using extracts from Rhazya stricta (R.S). Calotropis procera (C.P). and Calligonum comosum (C.C) to evaluate their potential as novel therapeutic agents.

pmc-12567437.title: Novel Multifunctional Cannabidiol-Based Analogues with In Silico, In Vitro, and In Vivo Anti-SARS-CoV-2 Effect
pmc-12567437.creator: Graziella dos Reis Rosa Franco, Vanessa Silva Gontijo, Flávia Pereira Dias Viegas, Matheus de Freitas Silva, Cindy Juliet Cristancho Ortiz, Caio Miranda Damásio, Isabella Marie Fernandes Silva, Thâmara Gaspar Campos, Erik Vinicius de Sousa Reis, Felipe Alves Clarindo, Thaís de Fátima Silva Moraes, M
pmc-12567437.description: Background/Objectives: COVID-19 was responsible for millions of deaths worldwide. This study aimed to identify substances with in vitro and in vivo effects against the SARS-CoV-2 virus. Methods: Compounds PQM-243 and PQM-249, two terpene-N-acyl-aryl-hydrazone analogues, were evaluated in vitro against SARS-CoV-2 to a antiviral activity and inhibitory effect against angiotensin converting enzyme 2 (ACE2).

pmc-12593801.title: Membrane-associated estrogen receptor α prevents the amyloid β-induced suppression of GIRK channel activity in hippocampal neurons from female mice
pmc-12593801.creator: Haichang Luo, Ezequiel Marron Fernandez de Velasco, Jaeyoon Kim, Praseuth Yang, Paul Mermelstein, Joseph V Bonventre, Paul S Cooke, Kevin Wickman
pmc-12593801.description: BackgroundAmyloid β oligomers (oAβ) are a key pathogenic driver in Alzheimer’s Disease (AD). Neuronal G protein-gated inwardly rectifying K+ (GIRK/Kir3) channels are important regulators of neuronal excitability and prominent somatodendritic effectors for inhibitory G protein-coupled receptors, including the γ-aminobutyric acid type B receptor (GABABR).

pmc-12604970.title: Systematic evaluation and platform construction of kinetics modeling for herbal extraction in phytomedicine
pmc-12604970.creator: Peng Xiao, Zhexuan Yu, Tianxue Chen, Li Yu, Yu He, Weifeng Jin
pmc-12604970.description: Graphical abstractKeywords: Kinetics model, Model evaluation, Modeling platform, Phytomedicine, Ultrasound-assisted extraction Introduction In recent years, phytomedicine has garnered increasing attention due to its multi-component synergistic effects and growing evidence-based validation [1,2]. Among the various factors affecting therapeutic efficacy, the efficiency of active component extraction plays a pivotal role [[3], [4], [5]].

pmc-12648556.title: An incidental situs Inversus Totalis in a Pediatric case of granulomatous Panuveitis. A case report
pmc-12648556.creator: Carlos Eduardo Solórzano Flores, Daniel Aguilar, Fabiola Langner-Salinas, Carolina Hovelmeyer Jurgens, Diya Mehta
pmc-12648556.description: Situs inversus totalis (SIT) is a rare congenital abnormality characterized by a mirror-image transposition of thoracic and abdominal organs. Although SIT is a recognized congenital anomaly, it is often unfamiliar to physicians because it is typically asymptomatic and discovered incidentally.

pmc-13095908.title: SMILE body project: protocol for a randomized controlled trial of an online eating disorder prevention program in young women with psychiatric disorders
pmc-13095908.creator: Caroline Bruun Abild, Eric Stice, Pernille Byrial, Gry Kjaersdam Telléus, Loa Clausen
pmc-13095908.description: AimYoung women with psychiatric illness have an increased susceptibility for eating disorders (ED); however, no prevention initiatives have been tested for this group. The Body Project ED prevention program has produced promising effect on ED symptoms, body satisfaction, and future ED onset; however, no studies have investigated this specific vulnerable group.

pmc-13157369.title: Bio and Geno-toxic Activities of Cadmium- Arsenic Salts Combination And/or Fluoride in Female Rats Confirmed by Molecular Docking
pmc-13157369.creator: Doaa S. Foda, Noha E. Ibrahim
pmc-13157369.description: Heavy metals are increasingly recognized as major toxic agents and potential carcinogens. This research was designed to assess the biochemical and genetic toxicity that arises from the exposure to a combination of cadmium and arsenic salts and/or fluoride in rats over a period of two months.

pmc-13339529.creator: Clara Faria, The OxWell Study Team, Mina Fazel, Emma Soneson, Tamsin J. Ford, Simon White

BackgroundAccurate population prevalence estimates of eating difficulties in children and young people provide essential information for the design and implementation of prevention efforts. pmc-13623136.creator: Shauna A Rasmussen, Catherine M Lemons, Madelyn M Seemiller, Sabrina R Dallas, Milan Cambon Ledesma, Yuhan Wu, Lauren E Anshen, Ashlyn Farnham, Olivia S Garrett, Judith L Fridovich-Keil, Marisa S Bartolomei

pmc-13678125.title: Animal models for investigating post‐stroke cognitive impairment: A neurovascular trafficking perspective
pmc-13678125.creator: Pratchaya Kaewkaen
pmc-13678125.description: Post‐stroke cognitive impairment (PSCI) is a major cause of long‐term disability after ischemic stroke, yet its mechanisms remain incompletely explained by infarct volume, lesion location, or conventional vascular risk factors alone. Animal models are indispensable for clarifying how ischemic injury evolves into delayed cognitive dysfunction and for determining which mechanisms are experimentally tractable, reproducible, and translationally relevant.
